Swole
SWOHL
adjective (Millennial slang)
A dialect form of swollen (via swoll), used in AAVE and bodybuilding slang from the 1990s for very muscular, pumped up. It spread in 2000s–2010s gym culture and internet humour ("Do you even lift, bro?", "get swole"), and with the "swole doge" meme of the 2020s. Related: jacked, ripped, yoked, gains.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

To be swole is to be big, muscular, pumped: the product of heavy lifting and many protein shakes. "He got swole over the summer." The Christian observation: strength is a good gift, and training the body is not a sin. Scripture admires strong men: David’s mighty men, Samson’s God-given strength, the craftsman’s arms. Paul uses athletic discipline as an image of the Christian life: "I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection" (1Co 9:27). And he grants that "bodily exercise profiteth little" (1Ti 4:8): little, but not nothing. A young man who lifts to be strong for work, protection, and service is stewarding his body. The examination concerns the heart. Gym culture easily becomes a religion of the body, with its own liturgy, diet laws, and confessions, and its own idol: the mirror. Scripture deflates that worship: the LORD "delighteth not in the strength of the horse: he taketh not pleasure in the legs of a man. The LORD taketh pleasure in them that fear him" (Psa 147:10-11). Samson, the swolest man in the Bible, was undone by his appetites, and his strength was a gift on loan. A father lifts with his son and teaches him to be strong, disciplined, and humble: strong to carry the weak, disciplined in body as an image of discipline in soul, and humble enough to know that the strength comes from God and that godliness profits far more.

Webster 1828 Definition

Millennial gym slang (1990s AAVE and bodybuilding, from swollen) for very muscular; strength and training are good stewardship (1Co 9:27), but the LORD delighteth not in the legs of a man, and the body can become an idol (Psa 147:10-11).

SWOLE, adj. (AAVE and bodybuilding slang, 1990s; Millennial gym culture, 2000s–2010s; from swollen) Very muscular; pumped up from training. "Get swole." Related: jacked, ripped, gains.

No Webster 1828 entry located for the root swell in the online edition.

Decode for parents: encourage strength and discipline; watch for the mirror becoming an altar.

Key Scripture

1Co 9:27 — "But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway."

1Ti 4:8 — "For bodily exercise profiteth little: but godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come."

Psa 147:10-11 — "He delighteth not in the strength of the horse: he taketh not pleasure in the legs of a man. The LORD taketh pleasure in them that fear him, in those that hope in his mercy."

Jdg 16:17 — "That he told her all his heart, and said unto her, There hath not come a razor upon mine head; for I have been a Nazarite unto God from my mother's womb: if I be shaven, then my strength will go from me, and I shall become weak, and be like any other man."

Isa 40:31 — "But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint."

Modern Corruption

Swole celebrates strength, a good gift; gym culture can make the body an idol and the mirror an altar, which Scripture deflates: the LORD takes pleasure in them that fear Him.

expand to see more

The corruption is body-worship. Lifting can become an identity, a moral system, and a source of pride, with hours in the mirror and a hierarchy of men by size. It can also slide into dangerous shortcuts, steroids and extreme diets, and into contempt for weaker men. Samson’s story is the warning: "if I be shaven, then my strength will go from me" (Jdg 16:17). He thought the strength was his; it was always the Lord’s.

The recovery is strength as service. A strong body is a tool for work, protection, and helping others, and training it is a lesson in discipline that serves the soul. Teach young men to lift for strength and health, to stay humble, and to wait on the One who renews strength: "they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles" (Isa 40:31).

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old English swellan (to swell) → swollen → dialect swoll → 1990s AAVE and bodybuilding swole → 2000s–2010s gym and internet slang.

2000s–2010s: gym memes, "Do you even lift?"; 2020s "swole doge"

Biblical anchor: I keep under my body (1Co 9:27); he taketh not pleasure in the legs of a man (Psa 147:10)
